links.outcome: Quality of informed advice (rated score) and hallucination proportion
links.effect: Informed advice mean 9.30 (SD 4.42) vs mean 13.79 (SD 5.70), P<.001; hallucinations 97/120 (80.8%) vs 53/120 (44.2%), P<.001 (as reported)
links.quote: The best fine-tuned model significantly outperformed the original Llama2 model at providing informed advice (mean 9.30, SD 4.42 vs mean 13.79, SD 5.70; P<.001) and mitigating hallucinations (97/120, 80.8% vs 53/120, 44.2%, P<.001).

links.comparator_used: Best fine-tuned model alone, without retrieval
links.outcome: Response quality score and hallucination proportion
links.effect: Mean 13.08 (SD 5.43) vs mean 15.14 (SD 4.64), P=.001; hallucinations 71/120 (59.2%) vs 57/120 (47.4%), P=.02 (as reported)
links.quote: Incorporating information retrieval from reliable sources, particularly ophthalmology textbooks, further improved the model's response compared with solely the best fine-tuned model (mean 13.08, SD 5.43 vs mean 15.14, SD 4.64; P=.001) and reduced hallucinations (71/120, 59.2% vs 57/120, 47.4%, P=.02).
